Maya (sec): FYI — pen tester reported a KMS session token exposure during workload replay. Attaching their repro notes.
Samir (infra): Can you paste the exact steps they used? I want to see if it's a client-side leak or a server-side auth config.
Jenna (pen-test): Here are condensed repro steps from the engagement: 1) initiate bulk inference with `session_id` header 2) interrupt at ~10s 3) replay requests via curl with captured cookies 4) observe `x-redwood-session` value returned in `Set-Cookie` once the backend error path triggers.
Rachel (qa): We attempted to reproduce locally on staging and saw `Set-Cookie` only when the request routing failed to the fallback instance. Not seeing token in body, only cookie.
Kyle (sre): @Samir @Alex this sounds like a race where the backend fallback handler writes a cookie for legacy sessions. That shouldn't emit KMS-wrapped tokens. Do we have the payload/log evidence?
pen-test-bot: Uploaded: https://files.redwood.internal/pen/engagement-20260301/replay-logs.tgz (sha256: abc123...)
Jenna (pen-test): Included log excerpt in the bundle. Here's the relevant line (sanitized):
```
2026-03-01T14:22:05Z ERROR handler.go:232 writeFallbackCookie user=acct-9387 cookie="x-redwood-session=eyJraW..." route=/v1/generate err=timeout
```
Alex (eng-rt): That cookie value looks like a JWT-ish blob, but we never sign session tokens with KMS-wrapped material, only access tokens. Need to verify if this is PII or a session identifier.
Maya (sec): The pen report flagged it as high because they claimed token could be replayed to access customer data. We need to validate: is that cookie usable to call APIs, or is it just a short-lived frontend session?
Samir (infra): Quick check — our auth flow stores ephemeral session references in Redis; real API auth requires an `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` header. Cookies are used for Console UX only. If the fallback wrote a raw auth token that's bad.
Rachel (qa): I spun up staging with verbose auth logging and reproduced: when fallback handler hits `ErrBackendUnavailable`, it called `legacyCookieWrite()` which grabs `sessionRef` and `expiry`. The cookie contains only `sessionRef` (opaque id). Example cookie payload: `sr=8f7a..; Expires=...; HttpOnly; Secure`. No API key material.
Jenna (pen-test): The tester says they swapped the cookie into an API call header and got 401. They only demonstrated the cookie returned on error paths not covered in normal tests. They flagged retention of that log line (with truncated cookie) as a compliance gap because logs are kept for 180 days and include session refs.
Maya (sec): Two issues then: 1) Is there any chance session refs map to unencrypted long-term keys in KMS/HSM? 2) Are we logging sensitive identifiers longer than policy allows?
Alex (eng-rt): Session refs are stored as Redis keys that point to ephemeral grants; the grants contain pointers to policies but not raw secrets. KMS is used only for encrypting stored model artifacts and customer keys, not session refs.
Kyle (sre): On retention: logs for `handler.go` are in the app logs retention bucket (180 days). Compliance policy requires rotation/anonymization for user-identifiable session refs after 30 days for dev logs. This was missed for the pen engagement route because it was added via an internal flag `--enable-fallback-verbose`.
Samir (infra): Proposed remediation: 1) patch fallback handler to not write cookies in error path 2) scrub session refs from logs at emit-time (regex) 3) run a retest to confirm we don't return cookie or leak identifiers.
Maya (sec): Also need evidence: sanitized reproducer run + log archive demonstrating cookie no longer appears, plus a small audit that KMS/HSM keys were not referenced in these flows. Jenna — can you retest after the patch?
Jenna (pen-test): Will retest tomorrow. I'll attach test script and 2 runs: pre-patch (evidence) and post-patch (validation). I'll also score severity based on exploitability if post-patch still returns cookies.
Rachel (qa): I'll create a quick unit test and integration test to cover the fallback path and verify header/cookie behavior. Pushing a branch now: `fix/fallback-scrub-cookie-1776`.
Samir (infra): I'll coordinate a short deploy to staging once the branch is ready. Also will run a log-scrub job to redact session refs older than 30 days in dev logs.
Maya (sec): For compliance docs, we should note: KMS/HSM not used in session ref lifecycle; audit logs for key operations remain in KMS audit trail (we can export that), and we'll include a signed statement from infra confirming no long-term secrets were exposed.
Jenna (pen-test): Good. If you can point me at staging when deployed I'll run the replay. If everything is clean I'll mark the finding as remediated. If not, we'll escalate severity. :+1:
Kyle (sre): Tagging follow-ups: #1 deploy staging patch, #2 run redaction job, #3 pen retest, #4 produce remediation evidence bundle.
Maya (sec): Thanks all — please paste links to PR, deploy, and retest log bundle in this thread so we have an audit trail.
Samir (infra): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/420 (WIP)
Rachel (qa): Integration run started at 2026-03-02T09:12Z, will post logs when done.
Jenna (pen-test): I'll schedule retest window 2026-03-02 16:00 UTC. If anyone can't make it, post availability.
Alex (eng-rt): Quick note: even if cookie is opaque, we should avoid logging it in error stacks. I've added a `redactCookie()` helper in the branch.
Maya (sec): Solid. Closing loop once Jenna confirms. Please remember to include the KMS audit export for the time window Jenna used.
Jenna (pen-test): Received, will verify KMS logs show no access related to these session refs.
Kyle (sre): Closing with action items in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
